title: Composition of rational compact-support functors on localizing constructible categories
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of positive characteristic different from $\ell$, and separated finite-type $k$-schemes $X,Y,Z$, as in [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Fix an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ and a finite intermediate extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $\Lambda=E$ or $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, with the pulled-back condensed coefficient sheaves, including the finite-subextension-valued convention at $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, of [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring; sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]. Write $\Dbc(T,\Lambda)$ and $\Dctf(T,\Lambda)$ for the bounded constructible complexes and those of finite Tor amplitude in $D(\Mod_{\Lambda_T})$ [sk-def-sfb-constructible], and $\mathcal T_T=\Loc(\Dctf(T,\Lambda))$ for the localizing closure [sk-def-localizing-closure]. For separated finite-type $k$-morphisms $X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{g}Z$, let $Rh_!:\mathcal T_{\mathrm{source}(h)}\to\mathcal T_{\mathrm{target}(h)}$, for $h=f,g,gf$, be the functors of [sk-prop-sf-existence], formed from $Rr_*j_!$ for compactifications $h=r\circ j$, with $j$ a quasi-compact open immersion and $r$ proper, identified for different compactifications by the comparison isomorphisms of [det-sf-comp-coherence-cocycle]. There is a natural isomorphism
$$
Rg_!\circ Rf_!\xrightarrow{\sim}R(g\circ f)_!:\mathcal T_X\longrightarrow\mathcal T_Z,
$$
compatible with the compactification comparison isomorphisms. In particular the isomorphism is independent of the chosen compactifications.

proof.text: Use compactification_localizing to supply all three preservation witnesses. The rational coefficient disjunction is a subcase of the corrected admissible coefficient predicate.
Take one ambient composition isomorphism from the model lemma and lift it to the full localizing target. Lift the three compactification cocycles to the full subcategories.

For arbitrary triples define alpha by whiskering the comparisons to the fixed triple, applying its composition isomorphism, and comparing to the chosen composite endpoint. Naturality and the three cocycle equations prove the simultaneous comparison square. This is the proved Lean transportComposition lemma.

The cocycle normalization with a dense refinement and its identity identifies each comparison component with its prescribed refinement component, using the identity lemma. Substitute these three equations into the transport square and apply the full-subcategory inclusion.

proof_origin.place: Composition construction followed by cocycle transport; no claim of the additional open-normalized composition or associativity is made by this item.
